classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish a lateral edge from a face slant height and identify the appropriate horizontal distance for each pyramid height.

content.prompt: There are different ways to approach finding the height of a pyramid depending on what information is given. For each of the following square-based pyramids, find the exact length of the diagonal of the base and the height of the pyramid to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Square-based pyramid, apex vertically above the marked base centre. Black visible edges and dashed hidden edges; red dashed height and base diagonal. The 4 cm label belongs to the lateral edge, and the 2 cm label to a base edge. Decorative source blue outlines are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Square base side 2 cm; lateral edge 4 cm; altitude meets the centre of the square. Equal double ticks on adjacent base edges.
spec.answerVisibility: Given lengths and construction lines only.

answer.worked:
Let $d$ be the base diagonal and $h$ the perpendicular height, in centimetres.
$$\begin{aligned}d^2&=2^2+2^2\\d&=\sqrt8\\h^2&=4^2-\left(\frac{\sqrt8}{2}\right)^2\\h^2&=14\\h&=\sqrt{14}\approx3.74\end{aligned}$$
The base diagonal is $\sqrt8\text{ cm}$ and the height is $3.74\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Square-based pyramid with 5 cm front base edge and a 6 cm face slant height from the apex to the midpoint of the right base edge. A leader arrow targets the slant-height segment, distinct from the lateral edge. Black outlines and dashed hidden edges; red dashed altitude and base diagonal.
spec.mathematics: Base side 5 cm; face slant height 6 cm; perpendicular height ends at the marked base centre. Centre-to-midpoint distance is half a base side.
spec.answerVisibility: Given lengths, equality ticks, leader and construction lines only.

answer.worked:
Let $d$ be the base diagonal and $h$ the perpendicular height, in centimetres. The distance from the base centre to the midpoint of a base edge is $\dfrac52\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{aligned}d^2&=5^2+5^2\\d&=\sqrt{50}\\h^2&=6^2-\left(\frac52\right)^2\\h^2&=\frac{119}{4}\\h&=\frac{\sqrt{119}}2\approx5.45\end{aligned}$$
The base diagonal is $\sqrt{50}\text{ cm}$ and the height is $5.45\text{ cm}$.
